If you visit Charlotte and like the club scene, don't miss it!

I usually go to Texas de Brazil but I thought I would give Fogo de Chao a try.  My husband ordered an ice tea and it tasted terrible, very bitter.  He asked if he could exchange it for a diet coke and waiter came back and told us that he would have the charge him for both the ice tea (that had one sip missing) and the diet coke.  In my opinion, that's just poor customer service.  In the end the meal was okay.  The salad bar was okay but not too impressive.  In my opinion, I would rather go to Texas de Brazil.  The atmosphere, food, and service are better.

Ok, I read the reviews of this place. Seemed pretty mixed. When my mail person suggested them, I thought...ok, personal recommendation. I took my new-to-me small apso-poo dog, about 1.5 yo,  to them on Monday, I think it was, july 22.  I've had him two weeks. I cut out most of the mats. I said no perfume and no bandana and to cut it as is appropriate. He needed most of his hair off due to the person before me never having him groomed.

There are two listings here on Yelp.  However, if you check Winco's website the address they show is THIS one (Power Rd), not the Hampton address.  So I'm putting my review here.

This building used to be Costco.  Costco moved about a mile down the road, and Winco moved in.  Winco reminds me of Food4Less.  Same basic layout, and I don't think Food4Less took credit cards either.  Plus you bagged yourself, just like Winco.

The prices here are mostly reasonable.  You can do better in a regular grocery if you shop the sales, however.  For everyday prices these guys are a little lower, and I think at least some of that is the 5% (approximately) that they save by not accepting credit cards (VISA and those all charge a percentage of every transaction, which stores pass on to us).  Factor that in and this place probably isn't any better than Basha's or Fry's, and not as good as Costco.

Don't get me wrong, it's not a bad store.  But I wouldn't make a special trip here unless they had some great sale or coupon (which they did for their grand opening).  They are more hype than anything really special.

And, just to emphasize, they DON'T take credit cards.  Be aware of this, because they don't have it posted anywhere except at the registers.  By then you've already finished your shopping.  If it weren't for this I'd probably have granted three stars.

Tonight was an impromptu visit to a new place I haven't Yelped before.  What a treat!  I heard this place was located next to Bachi Burger and I also heard that they were owned by the same peeps.  Lastly, I heard the ramen was good.  All the reasons to try it out!

For my impromptu meal, I got the Tonkotsu ramen for $8.00.  With tax and tip, it came to about $11 which was a good deal!   The noodles are skinnier than what I'm used to but totally my preferance.  It's served in a big bowl with Chashu or roasted pork, green onions, bamboo shoots, seaweed and a nori square, all in a pork bone, milky-type broth. The broth was hot and great for cold nights, however, I wasn't too crazy for the broth, unfortunately.  As I sipped it, I kind of thought the broth made by the top ramen pork flavor packet tasted better.  I definitely apologize for comparing the two.  I do appreciate the fact that the broth is completely homemade.  I guess it might be a little too complex for my palate.  Here's what I love:  The Chashu.  The pork slices had a great meat to fat ratio and were super flavorful.  I also LOVE when ramen is accompanied with the light flavor of green onions.  LOVE, LOVE, LOVE the actual contents of the soup.

All in all, I had a great experience.  The broth preferance aside, I feel like it's a great place to visit if you're in the Windmill/Bermuda area.  I might just be crazy for comparing homemade broth to a store bought $0.25 manufactured packet broth, so you definitely need to get down there and try it out for yourself.

Pro tip: Do not ever under any circumstances use Joe's for mechanical work.  They do tires okay, but this business has gone to pot in the last year or so.  I took my car into Joe's as Big-O Tires told me I had a leaking rack and pinion and needed a new tire.  I figured this would be a one stop shop.  I have a very common tire so it can't be that hard to keep them on hand.  When we got to Joe's, we were told they didn't have my tire in stock and would need to order it new at $80 a pop.  We opted to have them do the rack and pinion anyway as I didn't feel safe driving my car to another (third) location for this work.  

BIG MISTAKE.  

They did indeed replace the rack and pinion but did a very sloppy job installing it and what should have been a 3 hour job took them a day and a half - first saying it would be done at 9am, then 1pm, then 3pm.  Nobody said anything to us about needing new lower control arms, but on my drive home, my car was still driving like crap so I turned around and called Joe's.  The mechanic tells me "I did what you told me to do.  I replaced the rack and pinion.  Maybe something else is wrong."  Again, they had this opportunity to tell me that my control arms were bad but failed to do so, especially since they KNEW about the problem. 

I took the car to Tire Pros, where they got the alignment done, and asked them who didn't do their job.  Not only did THEIR mechanic remember my car without putting her on the rack but they immediately told me that they had told Joe's about my bad lower control arms.  The mechanic at Joe's failed to call me and let me know.  They also showed me just how sloppy of a job this had been, cleaned it all up, and verified that these were my only problems remaining.  I ended up having to pay Tire Pro's to replace the control arms, fix the rack and pinion, and rotate my tires.  I lost my car for two days due to negligence at Joe's.  

After all these years of excellent customer service from Joe, he's officially lost a customer.  I caution everyone thinking of using these guys that their shop has really become incredibly unprofessional in recent years.

Just South West of Edinburgh lies a range of hills called the Pentlands, stretching 20 miles, across to Biggar. It's hard to review a geographical feature in itself (though they are undoubtedly beautiful) but you can say something about their effect. Being right outside Scotland's capital, the Pentlands make a great opportunity to escape the city and get some proper fresh air. As someone who grew up in the country, I really appreciate this.

This park doesn't feature some of the biggest or most challenging hills in Scotland, the tallest being Scald Law with an elevation of just under 580m, but this adds to its less daunting charm. The Pentlands is popular amongst amateur and professional hill walkers and those just out for a stroll as well as mountain bikers, dog walkers and others. There are many many routes to take, but if you are approaching from Edinburgh, unless you stray too far, you can't really get too lost, especially during the summer when there tends to be quite a lot of walkers about. This can be an issue for some and I know others prefer quieter, more secluded parks to walk.

You can easily get a bus out to the Pentlands. I would recommend taking the number 40 bus to Bonaly, or the McEwans 100 to Flotterstone. Once you're there is pretty obvious which way to walk to soon be into the Pentlands, although obviously there are a number of exact starting location depends on where you want to walk.

Details of specific walks as well as further information can be found on the website.
